title: Priority signal admission and circuit hysteresis safety to contain hosted 5xx waves during customer escalations
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: During a multi-tenant surge on 2025-02-16 we observed correlated 5xx spikes and timeout storms driven by connection-pool exhaustion and amplified client retries. Several customers escalated to CS/SEs requesting immediate relief. This ticket implements a short-lived, low-risk mitigation composed of (1) telemetry-driven admission signals to prioritize and smooth admissions, (2) tuned per-tenant circuit hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping, and (3) an idempotency verification patch at the edge to reduce replay storms. The goal is to stop 5xx amplification, protect latency SLOs for unaffected tenants, and provide a safe rollback path.

Reproduction: Load generator scenario A (linked) reproduces: - steady baseline at 200rps - tenant surge to 6k rps with multipart uploads and unbounded client retries - observe host-level connection pool depletion -> 502/504 cascades -> SDK retries amplify to 3x.

Impact: External: 5 major customers reported increased error rates and time-to-first-byte degradation (~3–8s tail latency). Internally: P99 latency + token cost increased by ~20% for the affected cluster. Customer escalations resulted in two Priority-1 incidents (PD alerts).

Proposed mitigation plan (phased):
1) Emergency patch (hotfix, <=2 hours to roll): gate inbound request admission using a lightweight telemetry signal. The admission controller will label requests with a priority score (tenant severity + recent error-rate delta + token size) and apply a probabilistic admission when pool utilization > 70%. This is not a permanent rate limit—it's a smoothing mechanism to avoid abrupt drops.
2) Circuit hysteresis tuning (safe rollout): increase the hysteresis/dampening window on per-tenant circuits from 30s -> 120s and add a decay function that reduces oscillation when recoveries are noisy. This prevents immediate re-enablement when transient success is observed.
3) Edge idempotency verification: add validation to the front proxy for idempotency tokens and detect duplicate in-flight requests (soft-fail to allow non-idempotent traffic). This reduces replay storms from misbehaving SDKs.
4) Dedicated fallback bridge (targeted): for customers with Dedicated eligibility flags, implement a fast-path to steer traffic to a reserved Dedicated pool when hosted admission drops below a threshold. This is opt-in and requires customer consent.

Rollout strategy:
- Hotfix: deploy to two canary pods in us-east-1 (5% traffic) for 30m with strict rollback on any >2% increase in 5xx.
- Circuit hysteresis: progressive rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with metric gates (p99 latency, 5xx rate, token cost).
- Idempotency validation: feature flag off by default; opt-in for internal canaries and one customer at a time.

Monitoring & success criteria:
- Primary: 5xx rate across cluster drops by >60% relative to peak within 30m of hotfix deployment for affected tenants.
- Secondary: tail latency stays within 10% of baseline for unaffected tenants; token cost delta <5% in 24h.
- Safety gates: if any customer reports increased error rate or if p99 latency for control tenants increases by >15% rollback immediately.

Testing:
- Unit tests for admission controller logic and statistical admission.
- Integration test using load-sim scenario A in staging with injection of retry amplification.
- Chaos test: simulate transient successes to ensure hysteresis prevents flapping.

Backward compatibility and SDK guidance:
- No wire-level change. SDK teams will be notified to ensure clients don't retry aggressively on 502/504; guidance doc and temporary recommended client-side retry backoff parameters included.

PR/Artifacts: links provided in links field.

Postmortem steps / follow-ups:
- Within 72h create an incident postmortem linking traces and the final root cause analysis.
- Consider longer-term investments: adaptive admission using model-predicted surge signatures, per-tenant KV cache prioritization, and improved client idempotency surface (explicit token rotation guidance).
